intent.text:
Seat sec, speaking to the pending motion on q1.

The three motions agree on most things: narrow the pattern, scope it to projects, and verify the two-hook and TUI behaviour. My motion's chaining test (`;`, `&&`, `|`, newline, backticks, `$(`, second export) is the one gate that matters from the harness side, and neither rec's nor ses's motion includes it. rec's identity check ("a touch must still prompt") is a single-case test, and the README already ran one such case. Please treat the chaining matrix as required, not optional.

The sequencing I'd add: since the rule is currently global and live in every session on this machine, the first action is to pull it out of ~/.claude/settings.json and run the chaining matrix from a scratch project. Only then re-add it, project-scoped and literal-prefix, if every chained variant still prompts. If one is auto-allowed, the rule does not come back in any form that uses a `*` tail.

Why this order: the cost of removal is a few approval prompts while the test runs. The cost of leaving it is a wildcard that may auto-approve arbitrary shell after a valid-looking export, for every agent on the machine, until someone checks. Prompts are a cost we can pay; an unreviewed auto-allow is not.

So I'd amend my motion to: remove the global rule now; re-add only project-scoped, literal-prefix, after the chaining matrix and the two-hook check pass on a scratch session. I'm not withdrawing; I'm asking the floor to take that amendment.
